answers.l: Inherited from Multics, where ls was the short name for list.
It has to be a shell builtin: a child process can't change its parent's working directory.
GNU rm refuses 'rm -rf /' unless you add --no-preserve-root.
cp -a keeps permissions, timestamps and symlinks. Plain cp does not.
Within one filesystem it is a single rename(2). Across filesystems it copies, then deletes.
Process status. BSD flags (ps aux) and System V flags (ps -ef) both still work on Linux.
Disk free, from the filesystem’s point of view.
Disk usage. When du and df disagree, look for a deleted file a process still holds open.
The argument order trips everyone: ln -s TARGET LINK_NAME.
wc -l counts newline characters, so a final line without one isn't counted.
Bill Joy wrote it on an ADM-3A terminal, whose keys put arrows on h, j, k and l.
Thompson shell in 1971, Bourne shell in 1979. Today it is usually dash or bash in POSIX mode.
Substitute user. With no argument, it means root.
Its if= and of= syntax comes from IBM JCL's DD statement. Nicknamed 'disk destroyer' for a reason.
Prints your uid, gid and groups.
Translates characters. tr 'A-Za-z' 'N-ZA-Mn-za-m' is ROT13.
Job control. Ctrl-Z, then bg, and the stopped job keeps running in the background.
Brings a background job back to the foreground.
iproute2's replacement for ifconfig, route and arp.
Netcat. Reads and writes raw TCP and UDP: port scanner, chat server and file transfer in one.
Its own tagline: like sed for JSON data.
In 2024 a backdoor in liblzma was caught because Andres Freund noticed ssh logins taking 500 ms longer.
ripgrep. Skipping everything in .gitignore is half the reason it feels fast.
GitHub's command-line client.
Ken Thompson's line editor. Its g/re/p command gave grep its name.
An arbitrary-precision calculator language. It originally compiled down to dc.
A reverse-Polish calculator and one of the oldest Unix programs. It predates C.
Numbers lines.
Octal dump. It defaults to octal because its users thought in PDP-11 octal.
Paginates text for printing, with headers and columns. Still in coreutils.
Runs a command once, later. cron's one-shot sibling.
The C compiler. Usually a symlink to gcc or clang now.
The archiver behind static libraries (.a files). Every .deb package is an ar archive too.
The assembler.
The linker. The name comes from "loader".
Lists the symbols in an object file.
Socket statistics. netstat's faster replacement.
A faster, friendlier find.
Pipe viewer. Puts a progress bar on any pipeline.
Line printer. The System V way to print.
Midnight Commander, a two-pane file manager in the Norton Commander tradition.
'Fix command.' Opens your last command in $EDITOR and runs whatever you save.
vi's line-mode alter ego. vi is literally ex's visual mode.
Steam Locomotive. Punishes a mistyped ls with an ASCII train you cannot interrupt.
hexdump -C under a shorter name.
Traffic control. Shape, delay and drop packets on Linux.
ApacheBench. Hammers a URL and reports requests per second.
Magnetic tape control: rewind, skip files, eject.
System V's pager, from before less was more.
Turns backspace-underscore sequences into real underlines for your terminal.
"Call up" another system over a serial line. A UUCP-era relic.

nope.w: One letter. It shows who is logged in and what they are doing.
nope.cat: Three letters. Concatenate your way to the next answer.
